claims.claim: DataFlow defines reusable operators and pipelines and introduces a DataFlow-Agent that can translate natural-language requirements into executable data preparation workflows.
claims.notes: A research system with task- and evaluation-specific results; it is not the unverified DataEvolver name in the legacy article.

claims.claim: The DataFlow project repository describes operator generation, pipeline organization, execution and data-evaluation utilities.
claims.locator: README; project architecture and agent features
claims.notes: Repository APIs evolve; this article does not claim to have deployed the framework.

claims.claim: Data-Juicer publishes a configurable data processing framework for foundation-model corpora with reusable processing operators.
claims.locator: README; Data Processor and operator docs
claims.notes: Data-Juicer is distinct from DataFlow and from the article's conceptual release controller.

claims.claim: Apache Airflow's Dynamic Task Mapping creates task instances at runtime from upstream outputs rather than requiring static fanout at DAG parse time.
claims.notes: Behavior refers to the stable Airflow documentation at the cited URL; actual deployment requires a pinned version.

claims.claim: Dagster provides asset checks that test properties of data assets, with results associated with materializations and execution.
claims.notes: Asset checks are not a legal rights clearance system.

claims.claim: Datasheets for Datasets argues that dataset creation, contents, preprocessing, intended use and maintenance should be documented for transparency and accountability.
claims.notes: A transparency framework does not automatically certify data rights.

claims.claim: The teaching release gate blocks on any hard-governance violation; otherwise it requests review if retention or audit coverage falls below the configured thresholds.
claims.notes: This repository policy is an illustrative recommendation, not an Airflow/Dagster default or a statistically calibrated threshold.

claims.claim: A workflow's completion or successful exit status is not evidence that corpus correctness, legal rights, privacy and downstream utility are verified.
claims.notes: Governance and quality are separate review dimensions; actual authorization depends on organizational policy.

claims.claim: Reproducible candidate comparison should freeze the input data and evaluation protocol and version code/configuration before comparing curation strategies.
claims.notes: Recommended experimental discipline; not proof that the conceptual AI planner improves data quality.
